chunks: And ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has forbidden the intoxicant from every drink for our Shiʿah, and compensated them for that with mutʿah.

key_terms.شَرَابٍ: drink; here referring generally to beverages
key_terms.شِيعَتِنَا: our Shiʿah; the followers associated with the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.عَوَّضَهُمْ: compensated them; gave them something in exchange
key_terms.ٱلْمُتْعَةَ: mutʿah; temporary marriage as a lawful dispensation
key_terms.ٱلْمُسْكِرَ: that which intoxicates; any intoxicating substance in drink

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام say about intoxicants and mutʿah for the Shiʿah?
ai.summary: This hadith states that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, forbade intoxicating drinks to the Shiʿah. It also presents mutʿah as a lawful alternative granted in compensation, placing the report within the jurisprudence of halal and haram and marriage law.
